 Americans abroad may still need to file U.S. taxes. Here’s what to file, when and tools to help.
 Published Fri, Nov 13 2026 Jayna Rohslau CNBC Select Staff Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email An estimated 5.5 million Americans lived abroad in 2024, a 1.85% increase from the year prior, according to the latest numbers from the non-profit group Association of Americans Resident Overseas. That could mean more people will file their  taxes  to Uncle Sam from overseas during the tax season.
 Americans living overseas must file applicable U.S. taxes and submit any annual tax paperwork their country of residence requires. For first-timers, the process can feel overwhelming; depending on income, investments and account balances, they may have more forms to complete than U.S. residents. While tax season may seem far off, experts recommend starting early to give yourself time to understand the process and get your finances in order. 
 Often, expats and others living outside the U.S. don’t realize they owe a tax filing until it starts to cause real problems for them, said Ann Marie Regal, CEO and founder of financial planning firm Avrio Wealth, which works with Americans living abroad. 
 “They get a letter eventually that says, ‘We're going to freeze all of your assets because you haven't been tax compliant,’” she said. 
 Luckily, several tools can help. Here’s what you need to know about what to file, when you need to report, deadlines and tools to help you keep track of your taxes.

 Tools to help you keep track of your taxes
 Several software tools can make filing your tax return as an expat much easier. When choosing the one that is best for you, consider the following:
 Types of forms : Choose software that can help you file all forms applicable to your financial situation. 
 Level of assistance : Understand how much help you may need, and look for software that matches it. 
 Price : Choose a plan that fits your budget. 
 Specialization : Decide whether you prefer a company that focuses exclusively on expats or a larger, more general one. 
 Here are some of our favorite tax software companies that provide expat services. 
 H&R Block
 At Select, we recommend H&R Block for expats with uncomplicated returns with few deductions, credits or complicated reporting requirements such as foreign assets or state tax residency obligations. 
 It offers both independent and professional support options and will help you fill out Form 2555 for the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion and Form 1116 for the Foreign Tax Credit. Costs start at $124 for self-filing and $259 for filing with a tax advisor.

 What tax forms do you need to fill out? 
 Here are the tax forms you may need to file if you’re an American living abroad. 
 What you need to file will depend on your income, foreign investments, country of relocation, how long you've been there and U.S. state tax residency or assets.
 U.S. Individual Income Tax Return 
 Also known as Form 1040, this is the most common tax document filed and reports how much you earned during the year. 
 Foreign Earned Income Exclusion 
 Through this tax break, qualifying taxpayers can exclude up to $132,900 of eligible foreign earned income from federal income tax in 2026. Additionally, they may be able to deduct or exclude certain housing expenses. 
 To qualify, you must show that you earn income while working in another country and that your main home base is abroad. You’ll also generally need to show that you’ve lived in another country for an entire tax year or spent at least 330 full days in a foreign country during a consecutive 12-month period. 
 Foreign Tax Credit  
 To avoid paying taxes on the same income to two different countries, you may want to deduct the foreign income tax you paid from your U.S. tax return or claim Foreign Tax Credits (FTC). 
 You can usually save more money by claiming an FTC than by taking the deduction. That’s because it lowers your actual tax bill, rather than just reducing taxable income, according to the IRS . FTCs can typically be carried over from year to year but, in general, you’ll still need income in another country to use them. Credits you don’t use will typically expire after 10 years, and you may also apply them to the previous tax year. 
 “Use it or lose it,” said Peter Sengelmann, partner and director of international wealth management and investments at Creative Planning.
 Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts 
 Depending on your financial asset type and value, you may have to report the balances of your foreign financial accounts through FinCEN Form 114, a report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts. 
 You must file a FBAR if you have a combined balance of more than $10,000 across all foreign financial accounts at any given point during the year.
 Statement of Specified Foreign Assets 
 Depending on your financial asset type and value, you may have to file a Statement of Specified Foreign Assets — Form 8938 — alongside your federal tax return.
 For single Americans living abroad or married Americans filing separately, you typically must report foreign financial assets exceeding $200,000 at the end of the tax year or valued at more than $300,000 at any point during the year. Those thresholds double for married couples filing jointly.
 Expat tax forms
 Tax form Purpose 
 Form 1040 Report your total income and calculate how much U.S. federal income tax you owe 
 FinCEN Form 114 (FBAR) Report foreign financial accounts if their combined value exceeds $10,000 at any point in the year 
 Form 2555 Claim the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion and if eligible, the foreign housing exclusion or deduction (FEIE) 
 Form 1116 Claim the Foreign Tax Credit (FTC) 
 Form 8938 Report foreign financial assets over $200,000 if single or married filing separately or $400,000 if married filing jointly 
 Do I have to pay state taxes?  
 Every state has its own residency rules, and whether you owe state income taxes depends on where you lived and earned income during the tax year.
 Here are certain circumstances where you may need to file state taxes: 
 Rental income from property in a state
 Restricted stock units that are taxed as income
 When do you need to file? 
 Many expats get an automatic two-month filing extension, moving the deadline from April 15 to June 15.
 Keep in mind, though, that interest on unpaid income tax will start on the regular tax deadline of April 15, even if you submit by the June extension deadline.
 You may also qualify for special tax rules for a limited time — like exemption and grace periods — depending on the country, Sengelmann said. Some countries also have tax treaties to help prevent double taxation, which you may need to disclose through Form 8833.
 What to do if you've missed U.S. tax filings
 Americans who have failed to file or pay their U.S. taxes can still get back on track. 
 Through the IRS Streamlined Foreign Offshore, eligible taxpayers may be able to catch up on three years of federal income tax returns and six years of FBARs, plus applicable taxes and interest, if they certify that they did not willfully fail to comply. 
 If you don’t qualify for Streamlined Filing Compliance Procedures, you have other options to catch up on your taxes, such as filing delinquent or amended returns.
